//: The Worker's own code: `_lib/` and the handlers under `api/`,
`feeds/` and `insights/`.
It exists because renaming a file is only half of a
conversion. Wrangler's esbuild compiles this directory and
reads no tsconfig at all: it strips annotations without
resolving a single one of them. So a `.ts` here typechecks
NOWHERE unless something points a compiler at it, and a `.ts`
nothing checks is a `.js` wearing types, which is worse than
the `.js` it replaced because a reader now believes them.
`scripts/check-types.ts` runs this, and its CONFIGS list is
what says the second half happened.
Node's globals and nothing else. The Worker is not a browser
and it is not node either, but the overlap is what this code
uses: `fetch`, `Response`, `Request`, `URL`, `crypto.subtle`,
`TextEncoder`, `btoa`. A handler that wanted a document would
be a handler in the wrong place.
`allowJs` is ON while the conversion is unfinished, and it is
the one setting here with a date on it. Twenty-four files in
this directory were JavaScript; each one that becomes `.ts`
is checked from that moment, and the last one to convert is
what lets this turn OFF. Leaving it on afterwards would let
an untyped `.js` back in silently, which is the hole this
whole config exists to close.
